extraction_notes: Forward and reverse curves were digitized from the supplied vector plots without adding interpolated points; the grouped reverse curve explicitly includes DSK220 and the forward curve is specifically labelled DSK220.
Fig. 3 DSK220 curve is a typical forward curve at Tj=25 degC, pulse width=300 us, and 1% duty cycle; its y-axis is logarithmic and its plotted current is instantaneous forward current.

Fig. 4 DSK28-DSK220 dashed curves show instantaneous reverse-current magnitude versus percent of rated peak reverse voltage at Tj=25 degC and Tj=100 degC; plotted reverse-current polarity is represented as positive magnitude.

The electrical-characteristics table gives IR1 maximum 0.05 mA for the DSK210-DSK220 group at VR=VDC and TA=25 degC. The separate IR2 high-temperature maximum is 5 mA for the DSK210-DSK220 group at VR=VDC and TA=100 degC; it is not used as the reverse-current fit target.
Absolute-rating bounds for DSK220 are VRRM=200 V, VRMS=140 V, VDC=200 V, IF(AV)=2.0 A, and IFSM=50 A at TA=25 degC; these are limits, not fitted curve points. Source: p. 1 maximum ratings.
Typical junction capacitance is 80 pF at 4.0 V DC and 1 MHz, represented in the schema as 8e-11 F.
The datasheet publishes no reverse-recovery-time specification and no breakdown-voltage or breakdown-current specification. VRRM and VDC ratings are limits, not breakdown data.
